item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports history interventions as diagnostics of model dependence. *Demystifying Sequential Recommendations* (2025) searches for minimal discrete history edits that change recommendations, evaluating targeted and untargeted counterfactuals ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606)). A 2026 temporal-attribution benchmark includes BERT4Rec and reports stronger faithfulness for GradientSHAP and Integrated Gradients than raw attention. Its separately trained masking-robust probe addresses perturbation artifacts; that probe design would fall outside this task’s single-model diagnostic constraint ([preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201)). RecSys 2025 research also shows that arbitrary shuffling confounds user-order patterns with item availability; constrained shuffling prevents interactions from preceding an item’s first observed appearance ([study](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/)).\n\nSuggested adaptation: freeze each trained BERT4Rec model and candidate set; compare removing recent events, removing repeated-item or explicitly defined title/description-similar events, and permuting historical order. Calibrate deletion effects against repeated random deletions matched on deletion count, with separate controls for recency and item frequency where feasible. Measure paired candidate-rank changes, top-10 exits and recommendation overlap; report user-bootstrap confidence intervals and variation across perturbation draws. Distinguish item repetition from inferred semantic repetition, since neither establishes observed intent. Rebuild left-padded histories consistently, append the reserved MASK, and read its final nonpadding position. These are proposed controls, not a verified standardized protocol from the cited papers. Interpret effects as sensitivity of this fixed model: deletion also changes context length and positions, while shuffling can create implausible histories. Neither establishes causal user intent."}
